proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof of chart_integral_eq. Notation: 𝓛 := (ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝ^P) is the normed space of continuous linear maps. It carries its Borel σ-algebra (Mathlib instance `ContinuousLinearMap.instMeasurableSpace := borel _`). e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 for i < n.
1. (The Gram-determinant map is continuous on 𝓛.) Define G : 𝓛 → ℝ by G(L) := √det(⟨L e_i, L e_j⟩)_{i,j<n}. For a fixed vector v, evaluation L ↦ L v is a continuous linear map on 𝓛, and the inner product ℝ^P × ℝ^P → ℝ is continuous. So every entry L ↦ ⟨L e_i, L e_j⟩ is continuous, and L ↦ (⟨L e_i, L e_j⟩)_{i,j} is continuous into Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ with the product topology. The determinant is a polynomial in the entries, hence continuous (`Continuous.matrix_det`), and Real.sqrt is continuous (`Real.continuous_sqrt`). So G is continuous; Mathlib's `fun_prop` proves this continuity directly.
2. (The differential is Borel.) ℝ^P is complete and ℝⁿ carries its Borel σ-algebra, so w ↦ fderiv ℝ Φ w ∈ 𝓛 is Borel measurable for every function Φ (Mathlib `measurable_fderiv`). No differentiability hypothesis is needed: fderiv ℝ Φ w = 0 wherever Φ is not differentiable, and the set of differentiability points is Borel.
3. (Composition.) G is continuous between spaces carrying their Borel σ-algebras, hence measurable (`Continuous.measurable`). The function in the statement is w ↦ G(fderiv ℝ Φ w), a composition of measurable maps (`Measurable.comp`), so it is Borel measurable. ∎
key_steps: L ↦ √det(⟨L e_i, L e_j⟩)_{i,j} is continuous on ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝ^P: entries are continuous, det is a polynomial and sqrt is continuous (fun_prop).
w ↦ fderiv ℝ Φ w is Borel measurable for every Φ (measurable_fderiv, Borel instance on the space of continuous linear maps).
The Jacobian is the composition of the two, so it is measurable (Continuous.measurable.comp).
